title: Factor a chain map with K-flat source through a K-flat target
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention] and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every chain map $t:D^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ with $D^\bullet$ K-flat, there are a K-flat complex $N^\bullet$ and chain maps $u:D^\bullet\to N^\bullet$ and $c:N^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ such that $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $t$ is chain homotopic to $c\circ u$. Chain homotopic means that there are maps $h^i:D^i\to I^{i-1}$ with $t^i-(c\circ u)^i=d_I^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_D^i$ for every $i$. If every term of $D^\bullet$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $N^\bullet$ can also be chosen with flat terms.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat, including its final flat-terms assertion.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the site is small in the specified universe. In its homotopy category, [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] gives the distinguished cone triangle $D^\bullet\xrightarrow{t}I^\bullet\xrightarrow{j}C^\bullet\xrightarrow{\delta}D^\bullet[1]$. Use the actual cone complex and chain maps, with $C=\operatorname{Cone}(t)$ and $\delta=-p$ in the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0G7D, first two sentences of proof; Derived Categories, cone convention and homotopy-category triangulated structure

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to $C^\bullet$. Obtain a chain map $m:M^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ which is a quasi-isomorphism, where $M^\bullet$ is K-flat in the acyclic-total-tensor sense and every $M^n$ is flat. Its degreewise surjectivity is not needed. Put $g=\delta\circ m:M^\bullet\to D^\bullet[1]$, an actual chain map.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, choice of the resolution of the cone; Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution

proof.text: We will use shift stability in precisely the notion [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For $s=1,-1$, the total differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives a chain isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes K[s])\cong\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes K)[s]$: reindex the summand $F^p\otimes K^{q+s}$ and multiply it by $(-1)^{sp}$. The two differential terms agree because this multiplier changes by $(-1)^s$ when $p$ increases by one. The shift differential is $(-1)^s d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so its kernels and images are those in the shifted degrees. Thus $H^n(T[s])\cong H^{n+s}(T)$ by [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. For every acyclic $F$, the right side is acyclic when $K$ is K-flat; hence $K[1]$ and $K[-1]$ are K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, K-flatness of the second triangle; Definition 06YN and the total-tensor differential, expanded shift calculation

proof.text: Set $g=m\delta$, $W=\operatorname{Cone}(g)$, and $N=W[-1]$. The cone formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies $N^n$ with $M^n\oplus D^n$. The cone triangle of $g$ is distinguished by [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated]. Two inverse rotations give a distinguished triangle whose objects are $D[1][-1],N,M$; the shift comparison identifies its first object with $D$. For K-flatness, use the signed total-tensor shift comparison of step 3 to make $D[1]$ K-flat. For any acyclic $F$, the canonical signed isomorphism identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(g))$ with the cone of the induced map between $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes M)$ and $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D[1])$. Both are acyclic by K-flatness. The triangulated subcategory of acyclic complexes therefore contains their cone. This proves that $W$ is K-flat, directly in the independent-coefficient predicate [def-pc-kflat-complex]; step 3 then makes $N=W[-1]$ K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0G6C, proof: cone on the connecting chain map, rotated backwards twice; Tag 0G7D second triangle and Tag 07A3 cone closure

proof.text: In the homotopy category let $S$ be the cone triangle of $g$ and $T$ the cone triangle of $t$. The first square from $S$ to $T$ rotated twice commutes: its vertical maps are $[m]$ and the canonical comparison $[D[1]]\simeq[D][1]$, since $g=m\delta$. Apply TR3 [def-weil-triangulated-category] and [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] to obtain a triangle morphism. Inverse-rotate it twice and compose with the inverse of the canonical isomorphism from $T$ to its twice-rotated, twice-inverse-rotated triangle. The first component is an isomorphism. Transport the second component through the quotient-shift comparison $[N]\simeq[W][-1]$ and choose a chain-map representative $c:N\to I$ by fullness of the quotient functor. Likewise choose $u:D\to N$ representing the first arrow of the source triangle after its first-object isomorphism. The first square is exactly $[t]=[u][c]$; the quotient equality gives Mathlib's Homotopy from $t$ to $u\gg c$.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, morphism of distinguished triangles; TR3 applied after rotation

proof.text: Apply the exact localization $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ from [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated] to the preceding triangle morphism. Both image triangles are distinguished. Its first component is an isomorphism; its third component is $Q(m)$ composed with a canonical isomorphism and is invertible because $m$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to deduce that its second component is invertible. Transport through the quotient-shift comparison to see that $Q(c)$ is invertible. The exact characterization of quasi-isomorphisms inverted by the derived localization gives QuasiIso c. This is the derived-category alternative in Stacks 0G7D.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, parenthetical derived-category proof; Derived Categories Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle

proof.text: Use the existing explicit site-to-monoidal tensor comparison, siteSheafTensorRightIso of [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], to identify site flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] with exactness of tensorRight. Tensor symmetry also gives exactness of tensorLeft. The resolution gives these properties for $M^n$; the additional hypothesis gives them for $D^n$. Finite biproducts of categorical flat objects are flat, by the existing source-library finite-limit closure of the flat object property. The actual shifted-cone term has the canonical isomorphism $N^n\simeq M^n\oplus D^n$, obtained by shiftFunctorObjXIso, homotopyCofiber.XIsoBiprod, and the shift comparison for $D$. Transport flatness through this isomorphism and back through siteSheafTensorRightIso. Thus this same $N,u,c$ satisfies the flat-term implication, without any replacement of the model or maps.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, final assertion; explicit cone model as in Derived Categories Tag 0G6C and the definition of flatness

proof_origin.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat, using the explicit shifted cone and the derived-category alternative. F1 formalization on 2026-10-21: TR3 followed by inverse rotations, direct signed total-tensor cone and shift comparisons at independent universes, and the existing site-to-monoidal tensor comparison for flat terms.
